investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the eval runner never obtained a VM ID or a remoteState value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a total contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). As a result, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never produced a live agent, so vmIdPresent and remoteState were never written, and the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json (lines 256–259) could not be satisfied.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod’s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 133s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail, latencyMs=141927 — the check ran for ~142 s, well past the scheduler's unschedulable verdict, confirming no recovery occurred within the eval window.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner never reached the point of writing orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState because the pod never scheduled.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, consistent with the runner aborting before any evidence could be captured.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, pod stuck for 142s — confirms the capacity exhaustion affected a second independent probe attempt.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck for 144s — confirms a third independent probe attempt also failed, ruling out a transient single-pod anomaly.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the evidence was absent.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all three probe pods received the same Unschedulable verdict with 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', indicating zero remaining allocatable units on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes at the time of the eval run.

[Likely contributing] Existing remote agent VMs were not released before the eval ran — if prior agent sessions or leaked VMs are holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, new pods cannot be scheduled until those slots are freed.

[Possible] Node affinity or selector misconfiguration on the probe pod spec — 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by affinity/selector rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 peer-pod nodes. If the affinity is overly restrictive, even partial capacity loss on those 2 nodes causes total failure.

[Possible] Cluster autoscaler has not added a new peer-pod-capable node — if the cluster relies on autoscaling to expand kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, a delay or misconfiguration in the autoscaler would leave the resource exhausted until a new node joins.

[Lower likelihood] Eval cleanup (withCleanup) from a prior run did not fully delete the remote agent and its VM, leaving the kata.peerpods.io/vm slot occupied and unavailable for the next probe cycle.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod provisioned by the eval runner was stuck unschedulable: the Kubernetes cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node was available for any of the three eval pods. Because the agent pod never reached a running state, the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) could not return an agentId, and the subsequent state-polling step could not produce the required evidence fields orgId, agentId, readyState, or state. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

This is directly stated in the scheduler message across all three failing checks (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the pod requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 exhausted nodes. If the affinity configuration changed or nodes were drained/cordoned, the effective pool could have shrunk.

Tertiary — a prior eval run or external workload consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and did not release them before this eval window: the eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) but if a previous run's cleanup failed, leaked VMs could hold the resource.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the eval runner never obtained a VM ID or a remoteState value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a total contract validation failure.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). As a result, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never produced a live agent, so vmIdPresent and remoteState were never written, and the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json (lines 256–259) could not be satisfied.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod’s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 133s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: status=fail, latencyMs=141927 — the check ran for ~142 s, well past the scheduler's unschedulable verdict, confirming no recovery occurred within the eval window.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner never reached the point of writing orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState because the pod never scheduled.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, consistent with the runner aborting before any evidence could be captured.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, pod stuck for 142s — confirms the capacity exhaustion affected a second independent probe attempt.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck for 144s — confirms a third independent probe attempt also failed, ruling out a transient single-pod anomaly.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the evidence was absent.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all three probe pods received the same Unschedulable verdict with 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', indicating zero remaining allocatable units on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes at the time of the eval run.

[Likely contributing] Existing remote agent VMs were not released before the eval ran — if prior agent sessions or leaked VMs are holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, new pods cannot be scheduled until those slots are freed.

[Possible] Node affinity or selector misconfiguration on the probe pod spec — 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by affinity/selector rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 peer-pod nodes. If the affinity is overly restrictive, even partial capacity loss on those 2 nodes causes total failure.

[Possible] Cluster autoscaler has not added a new peer-pod-capable node — if the cluster relies on autoscaling to expand kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, a delay or misconfiguration in the autoscaler would leave the resource exhausted until a new node joins.

[Lower likelihood] Eval cleanup (withCleanup) from a prior run did not fully delete the remote agent and its VM, leaving the kata.peerpods.io/vm slot occupied and unavailable for the next probe cycle.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-14 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval produced zero evidence—all five required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing from the check result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM capacity on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918) calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers a pod requiring kata.peerpods.io/vm. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, the pod remained Unschedulable for 133–144 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out. This is a cluster infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-layer failure.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available peer-pod VM slots, leaving none for the eval pod. This is the primary cause supported by all three sibling check messages.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, permanently restricting scheduling to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, the cluster has no scheduling headroom for any additional remote agent pod.

Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent eval load: the feature registry registers remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime as sequential checks (infra/evals/status/features.json lines 183-185); if prior checks leave pods or VMs unreleased before the next check runs, capacity is not restored in time.

Peer-pod VM quota set too low for the production-api environment: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource limit on the 2 eligible nodes may be configured below the demand required by concurrent or back-to-back eval runs.

A passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime immediately after the failure window, with no change to cluster capacity, would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.
Evidence that the pod spec produced by createAgent does not request kata.peerpods.io/vm would disprove the link between the eval runner and the scheduling error.
Scheduler logs showing the pod was rejected for a reason other than resource insufficiency (e.g., admission webhook rejection, image pull failure) would shift the root cause away from VM capacity.
